 Sandisk (SNDK) Dropped, So What Is Behind Its Latest Move?
 Sasha Jovanovic Wed, November 11, 2026 at 6:11 AM EST 3 min read SNDK +13.20%

 Learn more Sandisk (SNDK) just posted first quarter earnings that sharply reshaped the story around the stock, reporting revenue of US$11.0b and net income of US$8.1b, along with fresh guidance for early 2027. 
 Despite Sandisk's huge 216.66% total shareholder return over the past year, momentum has reversed sharply. The stock is down 45.63% on a 30 day share price return as regulatory worries, AI demand uncertainty and competitive pressure reset expectations around how sustainable recent earnings power really is. 
 Scan how other AI and semiconductor plays are repricing after Sandisk's swing in sentiment by reviewing the hand picked 53 AI infrastructure stocks that are tied into the same storage build out story. 
 Sandisk just printed huge profits, yet the share price has been hit hard. Is this move really about cracks in the business, or has sentiment simply swung too far and pulled the valuation with it? 
 Most Popular Narrative: 59% Undervalued 
 Based on the analyst consensus Narrative on Simply Wall St, Sandisk's fair value sits at about $2,105 per share, well above the last close of $859.99. This frames the recent selloff against a still-upbeat long term earnings story built on AI driven NAND demand. 
 Rapid AI and cloud workload expansion is driving data center NAND exabyte growth at a pace well above overall supply. This positions Sandisk's enterprise SSD portfolio and deepening hyperscaler engagements to support sustained revenue acceleration and structurally higher pricing power, benefiting earnings. 
 See why 194 investors see Sandisk as 59% undervalued . 
 Result: Fair Value of $2,105 (UNDERVALUED) 
 Still, the bullish Sandisk narrative leans on tight supply and AI demand that could ease, while heavy BiCS8 and SSD investment risks underused capacity if forecasts prove too optimistic.
